Children don't need perfect parents. They need adults with direction and a clear voice.

Your child is growing up in a world where anything that can be memorized can be looked up. What's left can't be bought, downloaded, or delegated. It has to be trained, early, by someone who cares enough to do it.

The Most Important Thing You Can't Buy Your Child is not a parenting manual and not another book that gives parents a guilty conscience. It's about who your child becomes, and what you do to equip that person.

Don't wrap your child up. Unwrap them.

What you get

  • Ten mental muscles that don’t develop on their own but can be trained, from responsibility to hope
  • Ten concrete tools for each muscle, ready to use in everyday life, plus one small experiment per chapter that you can start tomorrow
  • Four developmental phases from infancy to young adulthood, and how your role changes along the way
  • Two chapters about the grandparents: one for them, one for you

With room for your own note

The book opens with a page for you, the giver: for, from, and because. And it ends with room for your own letter, the one you want the child to have, even twenty years from now.
